drafts.comparison: Index the combined family of every Y_1,...,Y_n and X_1,...,X_m by a disjoint sum of the two finite index types and impose iIndepFun on that whole family. This requires mutual independence across and within the two groups, stronger than independence only between the two vector-valued samples or pairwise independence of observations. It does not assert identical distributions, equality of the null and alternative laws, positive densities or absence of ties; those are separate source assumptions. Preserve both sample sizes and the raw-observation domain rather than substituting exchangeability of fitted scores.
drafts.gap: iIndepFun directly represents mutual independence of the entire combined observation family.

A disjoint index type includes both sample groups in one mutual-independence predicate without imposing identical distributions or no ties.
